methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective multi-cohort bioinformatics study combining four public datasets (TCGA training; GSE30219, GSE31210, FUSCC/EGAS00001004006 validation; total N=550) with machine-learning model selection via Mime1 across 10 algorithm families evaluated by C-index. Uses WGCNA + DEG intersection (548 core genes), single-cell validation (GSE189357, n=9), and in vitro knockdowns of DEGS1 and PLOD1. Limitations explicitly acknowledged: retrospective cohorts, limited scRNA-seq sample size, in silico drug predictions, and notably absence of nested cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning. Batch-effect correction via sva was applied for metacohort.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort-based prognostic model development and validation; maps to Oxford LoE 4 (case series/cohort without contemporaneous control). MAPI could help identify stage I LUAD patients at higher recurrence risk who may benefit from adjuvant therapy and proposes candidate agents (paclitaxel, bortezomib, vincristine), but all clinical implications require prospective validation. Directly addresses the gap that TNM stage alone under-stratifies stage I LUAD.

reporting_quality.justification: Prediction-model development/validation study; TRIPOD is the appropriate reporting framework. TRIPOD is not explicitly cited but the manuscript reports training/validation cohorts, model-selection process, C-index, AUCs at 1/3/5 years, multivariable Cox adjustment, subgroup analyses, and external validation in three independent cohorts. Missing items relative to TRIPOD include predictor handling, calibration plots (not shown beyond ROC), and explicit reporting of sample-size justification for development. Public data sources are named (TCGA, GSE30219, GSE31210, EGAS00001004006), supporting reproducibility; individual model coefficients are in supplement.

novelty_literature.justification: Metabolism-based prognostic signatures in LUAD have been published (Hu et al. 2021, Zhu et al. 2022), as cited. The specific novelty is (i) explicit focus on stage I LUAD, (ii) WGCNA-driven selection of metabolism-related genes from KEGG/REACTOME/Human-GEM combined with 10 ML algorithms and 101 combinations, (iii) integrated single-cell validation across AIS/MIA/IAC preneoplasia-to-invasive continuum, and (iv) functional wet-lab validation of DEGS1 and PLOD1. This is a meaningful extension rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear IMRaD narrative with a logical progression from WGCNA to model construction, validation, molecular characterization, immune/therapeutic analyses, single-cell validation, and functional confirmation. Figures are multi-panel but well-labeled, and tables and supplementary structure is referenced consistently. Some minor typographical and phrasing issues (e.g., 'immunologically activate') and the in silico drug-repurposing section could use clearer caveats inline rather than only in the Discussion.

key_strengths: Comprehensive multi-cohort validation (TCGA training; GSE30219, GSE31210, FUSCC validation) with batch-effect correction
Systematic ML model selection across 10 algorithms and combinations (Mime1 framework) with C-index-based selection
Single-cell validation across AIS/MIA/IAC continuum and in vitro knockdown of DEGS1/PLOD1 as functional support
Explicit focus on stage I LUAD, a clinically under-stratified population
key_concerns: Retrospective public-cohort study without prospective clinical validation; TRIPOD not explicitly cited and calibration metrics not presented
Hyperparameter tuning via nested cross-validation not performed (acknowledged by authors)
In silico drug-sensitivity predictions (GDSC, CTRP, CMap) require clinical validation before practice use
Sample size for scRNA-seq validation is modest (n=9)
No evaluation on independent prospective cohort or imaging-enriched datasets beyond the four public sources
chief_reviewer.rationale: A thorough multi-cohort prognostic-model study for stage I LUAD with WGCNA, machine learning, single-cell validation, and limited functional confirmation; tier 2 with minor revisions is appropriate given solid design but absence of prospective validation and formal TRIPOD compliance.
